page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-90 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on AMD EPYC 9B14 processors using the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 90 vCPUs derived from 45 dedicated physical cores with symmetric multithreading enabled. The CPU subsystem features 32 KB L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB L2 cache per core, and a 32 MB L3 cache. It incorporates advanced vector and cryptographic instruction sets, including AVX-512 (supporting VNNI and BF16 extensions), AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, while omitting AMX matrix accelerators.

The instance delivers 360 GB of system memory, maintaining a 4:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio with 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Benchmark results indicate substantial parallel throughput, with multi-core stress-ng scores reaching 129,160.54 and Geekbench multi-core reaching 19,922.0, both placing in the top 25%. Extended instruction performance is highlighted by a PassMark CPU score of 87,235.36 and a Clang software compilation score of 60,198.0, placing in the top 10%. Memory read bandwidth on large 256 MB blocks reaches 217.54 GB/sec, while write bandwidth stabilizes at 77.61 GB/sec.

Hardware tradeoffs include the complete absence of local storage and dedicated hardware accelerators, featuring zero GPUs and no bundled NVMe drives. External block storage must be provisioned independently for operational persistence. Single-threaded metrics, including a Geekbench single-core score of 1,884.0 and single-threaded gzip compression of 27.43 GB/sec, fall into the middle 50% tier, showing that processing gains are concentrated in high-concurrency environments rather than raw per-thread frequency.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c3d-standard-90 provides dense computational capacity suitable for horizontally scalable enterprise applications without the premium attached to specialized GPU hardware. Benchmark data shows strong performance in static web serving throughput (54.01 GB/sec) and Redis SET operations (118.12 million operations/sec). These metrics indicate effective alignment with large-scale multi-threaded workloads, including high-throughput web serving, large in-memory databases, CI/CD compilation clusters, and medium-scale CPU-based LLM inference pipelines.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-90 is a general-purpose virtual machine configured with 90 vCPUs across 45 dedicated physical AMD EPYC 9B14 cores on the x86_64 architecture. Supported by 360 GB of RAM at a standard 4:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio, the instance integrates AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI instruction sets. The server contains zero GPUs and includes no local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions. Benchmark measurements demonstrate top-tier multi-threaded processing, evidenced by high PassMark CPU marks, Clang software compilation scores, and robust in-memory Redis throughput, while single-core performance settles in the middle tiers. Given its dense compute allocation and strong memory read bandwidth, c3d-standard-90 is designed for multi-threaded enterprise workloads, distributed compilation farms, large in-memory caches, and multi-tenant application serving.
